imperative:*.why: يَنْبَغِي 'it is proper, it befits' is impersonal: it states what befits someone (يَنْبَغِي لَكَ, 'it befits you'), so no one can be told to do it — the command اِنْبَغِ is a mechanical form nobody uses.

present:1st.why: يَنْبَغِي is impersonal and used only in the third person (يَنْبَغِي, تَنْبَغِي, with the person in لِـ: يَنْبَغِي لِي 'it befits me'); أَنْبَغِي and نَنْبَغِي are not used.

present:2nd.why: يَنْبَغِي is impersonal and used only in the third person (with the person in لِـ: يَنْبَغِي لَكَ 'it befits you'); the second-person forms are not used.

past:1st.why: اِنْبَغَى 'it befitted' is impersonal and used only in the third person (مَا انْبَغَى لِي); اِنْبَغَيْتُ and اِنْبَغَيْنَا are not used.

past:2nd.why: اِنْبَغَى 'it befitted' is impersonal and used only in the third person (مَا انْبَغَى لَكَ); the second-person forms are not used.

present:*.why: تَبَارَكَ 'blessed (and exalted) is He' is a frozen verb said only of God and only in the past (تَبَارَكَ اللَّهُ, تَبَارَكْتَ رَبَّنَا); the lexicographers note that يَتَبَارَكُ is not said.

imperative:*.why: تَبَارَكَ 'blessed is He' is a frozen verb of praise used only in the past; it has no command — تَبَارَكْ is a mechanical form nobody uses.

كَادَ 'to be about to, almost' is a verb of approach (a sister of كَانَ) that only frames another verb (كَادَ يَسْقُطُ); it has a past and a present but no imperative — كِدْ is a mechanical form nobody uses.
زَالَ / يَزَالُ is the incomplete verb of مَا زَالَ, لَا يَزَالُ 'still, not cease to' (a sister of كَانَ), always used with a negation; it has no imperative — زِلْ is a mechanical form nobody uses.
خَفِيَ 'to be hidden' describes a state of its subject, not an act one can be told to do; the command اِخْفَ is not used (one says اِخْتَفِ 'hide!', from Form VIII).
حَبِطَ 'to come to nothing' is said of deeds and efforts that become void; it is not an act one can be told to do, so the command اِحْبَطْ is not used.
عَمِيَ 'to be(come) blind' describes what befalls its subject, not an act; the command اِعْمَ is not used.
عَمِهَ 'to wander blindly (in error)' describes a state of being lost, not an act one can be told to do; the command اِعْمَهْ is not used.
حَاقَ 'to befall, to close in on' is said of a punishment or a plot that overtakes someone (حَاقَ بِهِمْ); no one is told to befall, so the command حِقْ is not used.
ثَقُلَ 'to be heavy' is a faʿula verb of a lasting quality, not an act anyone can be told to do; its mechanical command اُثْقُلْ is not in use (one says كُنْ ثَقِيلًا).
تَمَّ 'to be complete' is intransitive and states that something came to its end; its mechanical command اِتْمِمْ is not in use (one says أَتِمَّ, the Form IV 'complete it!').
أَفَلَ 'to set' is said of a star, the moon or the sun going down (6:76–78); no one can be told to set, so its mechanical command اُؤْفُلْ is not in use.
نَفِدَ 'to run out, to be used up' is said of a supply coming to its end (18:109, 16:96); it is not an act, so its mechanical command اِنْفَدْ is not in use.
أَلِمَ 'to feel pain, to suffer' is a state that befalls someone, not an act anyone can be told to do; its mechanical command اِئْلَمْ is not in use.
